newsitem.title: GREECE: SALOMON UNDERWEIGHT ON GREEK SHARES SHORT TERM.
newsitem.headline: SALOMON UNDERWEIGHT ON GREEK SHARES SHORT TERM.

text.p: Greek equities have become expensive with a broad-based market price earnings ratio (P/E) of 12 and Salomon has reassessed its valuation to underweight short term and neutral long term, it said in its August strategy report on emerging Europe.

"We expect the market to be seasonally quiet in August while trading slows down during the summer holidays. For the rest of the year, we expect the market to continue to see a slight correction," said emerging Europe strategist Danielle Downing.

But Greece will probably still be among the top 10 best-performing emerging markets at the end of this year, the strategist said. It was a downgrade from its previous strategy report in July which had called for a neutral stance on grounds that valuations had been pushed to unattractive levels.
This year's market rally was driven by improving macroeconomic fundamentals, a pragmatic government and sharp cuts in interest rates.
EU-financed public investment has led to a real GDP growth rate of 2.9 percent -- slightly above 1996 figures.

"The issue of EMU convergence is still at the forefront for the Greek government and will push it to continue a tight fiscal austerity programme which is expected to take effect in 1998," the report said.

In a global context, Greece's equities market is still among the top five best-performing markets -- the IFCI Greek index has appreciated 40.4 percent in $ terms. But despite its overall outlook, Salomon issued a buy recommendation on OTE telecom noting that the share's valuation looked "undemanding".
"Given the substantial price gains of southern Europe's telephone operators over the past couple of years, the relative valuation of OTE to the sector looks compelling," said analyst Douglas Wight.
OTE shares trade on a prospective P/E of 11 times 1998 estimared earnings versus the sector average of around 16 times.
